title: Stage 2 — First End-to-End System
goal: Build one complete vertical slice: database, REST API, and frontend talking to each other.
summary: Your first full-stack feature: a SQL table, Express GET/POST endpoints, and a frontend that reads and writes through them.

checkpoint.prompt: You want to fetch the list of all workouts without changing anything. Which HTTP method fits?
checkpoint.explanation: GET reads data and should never modify state. POST creates, PUT/PATCH update, DELETE removes.

checkpoint.prompt: Write the SQL to read every column of every row from a table called workouts.
checkpoint.explanation: `SELECT * FROM workouts;` returns all columns (*) of all rows from the workouts table.

checkpoint.prompt: A POST request successfully creates a new workout. Which status code should the API return?

choices.text: 200 OK is the only correct option

checkpoint.explanation: 201 Created signals a new resource was made. 200 is fine for reads/updates; 404 means the resource doesn't exist.

checkpoint.prompt: After `const res = await fetch(url)`, how do you get the parsed JSON body?
checkpoint.explanation: `res.json()` returns a promise that resolves to the parsed body, so you await it.

checkpoint.prompt: Your frontend requests /workouts/999 and gets a 404. What does that mean?

choices.text: No workout with id 999 exists on the server
You are not allowed to see it

checkpoint.explanation: 404 means the requested resource wasn't found. A crash is 500; a permission problem is 401/403.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP method is conventionally used to create a new resource?
questions.explanation: POST creates. GET reads, PUT/PATCH update, DELETE removes.

questions.prompt: What is JSON's role in a typical REST API?

choices.text: A text format for sending structured data between client and server
A styling language for the frontend

questions.explanation: JSON is the lingua franca for request and response bodies — a lightweight, language-neutral data format.

questions.prompt: What is a primary key in a relational table?

choices.text: A column whose value uniquely identifies each row
The first column you happen to add

questions.explanation: A primary key (often an auto-incrementing id) uniquely identifies each row so it can be referenced reliably.

questions.prompt: What does a 500 status code indicate?

choices.text: An unexpected error on the server

questions.explanation: 5xx codes are server-side failures. 2xx is success, 4xx is a client error like bad input (400) or not found (404).

choices.text: One feature working through every layer: database, API, and UI
Finishing the entire database before touching the API

questions.explanation: A vertical slice proves the whole stack works together for one feature, instead of building each layer in isolation.
